name: Dalim
description: A star 14 parsecs away, 2.0 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 14879: radius 1.974 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 4.705 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.042) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 14879: effective temperature 6055 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.032)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 14879: distance 14.237 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.006), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 14 parsecs away, 2.0 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 4.705 times the Sun's luminosity at 6,055 K, so 1.974 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 14879: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Alpha Fornacis
quotes.card: Alpha Fornacis is a triple star system in the southern constellation of Fornax.
quotes.introduction: At a combined apparent magnitude of 3.92, it is the brightest star in the constellation and the only one brighter than magnitude 4.0.
